Maria Diatrix, 61, and her husband stood in front of a transfer passageway with three large suitcases, unable to get through the ticket gates because the QR code on their express train tickets was not being recognized. As crowds streamed through three separate passageways leading to Seoul Metro Lines 1 and 4 and the Airport Railroad, the couple stood helplessly in front of the gates. They pressed the assistance button, only to receive an announcement over the speaker advising them to exit via the second basement level or purchase new single-journey transit cards. Confronted with a complicated maze at what was supposed to be their first gateway to Korea, the couple did not know what to do. items.title: Foreign workers demand right to switch workplaces without letter of release
items.title_zh: 外籍劳工要求在没有解聘书的情况下有权更换工作场所
items.summary: Many foreign workers in Korea are stuck in their current jobs without the freedom to seek better employment, due to a regulation that a union of foreign language teachers wants abolished. For many foreign workers living in Korea on an E-series visa, their continued stay in the country is tied directly to their jobs. In the eventuality that they have to change jobs in the middle of a contract, they must seek consent from their employer through a document known as a letter of release. Korean employers effectively sponsor visas for foreign employees by guaranteeing their status in the country. This leaves foreign employees vulnerable to exploitation by employers, who wield disproportionate control over their working conditions, wages and even housing. By withholding a letter of release, employers can effectively trap workers in unfair or abusive workplaces, denying them the freedom to seek better employment and leaving them with little power to challenge mistreatment. items.summary: Lee Seung-jin won the Model High School Student award at the second Korea Multicultural Youth Award — now known as the Global Korea Award — in 2013. Three years later, he told The Korea Times his dream was to become an Air Force pilot. A decade on, the 29-year-old is living that dream. As a captain with the 19th Fighter Wing, Lee leads a flight of four F-16 fighter jets and helps defend Korea’s airspace every day. “I take pride in every mission because this is a job that not just anyone can do or is trusted with, and because I longed to be in this position,” Lee said in an interview with The Korea Times. Born to a Korean father and a Japanese mother, Lee grew up navigating two cultures — and it was that dual heritage that planted the seed of his ambition. “Flying to see my maternal grandparents in Japan was always thrilling, so I grew even more interested in airplanes. The hope of one day flying my parents to their hometown in a plane I pilot also motivated me,” he said. items.summary: A hacking attack on the Internet Post Office has exposed the personal information of at least 113,855 customers, with the full scope of the breach still under investigation, the postal service said Saturday. The Korea Post, under the Ministry of Science and ICT, said it has confirmed that hackers had accessed mailing records containing customers' personal information and is working to determine the full scope of the breach. The attackers accessed the mobile Internet Post Office's delivery location change service and viewed the names, addresses and phone numbers of recipients of registered mail being delivered between Nov. 17 and 24. An analysis of data from a single day alone found that 113,855 people had their information exposed. Korea Post said it became aware of signs of the breach on Wednesday and requested a police investigation. Korea Post temporarily suspended some services, including the delivery-location change function, and blocked access to its mobile website from overseas IP addresses. 2026, as well as progress made in implementing decisions adopted during the two meetings.Discussions focused particularly on establishing the alliance's institutional frameworks and the practical Secretariat in Saudi Arabia, emphasizing its important role in supporting institutional work and strengthening effective coordination among member states.The committee also reviewed the outcomes of ongoing political and military consultations and agreed to continue consultations aimed at strengthening cooperation and coordination on matters of mutual interest.It reaffirmed its support for efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and promote the peaceful settlement of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy.The committee reiterated its strong condemnation of the continued brutal Houthi attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.The three countries also renewed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in defense industries, joint technological development, training and capacity building.

items.title: Condemnations mount over attacks on Saudi Arabia following Houthi strikes on Jazan refinery and port
items.title_zh: 在胡塞武装袭击吉赞炼油厂和港口之后，对沙特阿拉伯的袭击的谴责声音日益高涨
items.summary: RIYADH — Kuwait, Bahrain, Algeria and the Muslim World League (MWL) condemned the continued attacks against Saudi Arabia, amid mounting condemnation of the Houthi attacks on the Jazan oil refinery and port. In a statement issued on Friday, Kuwait’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned and denounced the continued terrorist attacks by the Houthi militia against Saudi Arabia, including the attack on the Jazan oil refinery, which killed one worker and injured several others, as well as the attack on Jazan Port. The ministry described the attacks as a flagrant violation of the Kingdom’s sovereignty and a grave breach of international law and international humanitarian law. Kuwait stressed its categorical rejection of attacks targeting civilians, civilian objects and vital facilities, warning that such actions constitute a dangerous escalation and threaten regional security and stability, as well as the safety of global energy supplies. The ministry reaffirmed Kuwait’s absolute solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its support for all measures taken by the Kingdom to safeguard its sovereignty, security and stability. Bahrain also condemned attacks by the Iranian-backed Houthi terrorist militia against civilian and economic facilities and objects in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on the Jazan oil refinery, which killed a Nepali worker and injured others of various nationalities, and the attack on Jazan Port. Bahrain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also referred to attempted attacks targeting sites in Ras Tanura Governorate, the vicinity of Jeddah Islamic Port, Riyadh and other areas of the Kingdom, which were intercepted and thwarted by Saudi air defenses. The ministry stressed that the continued Houthi terrorist attacks using missiles and drones against civilian and vital facilities, including energy facilities and commercial ports, constitute a flagrant violation of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and the provisions of international law and international humanitarian law. It warned that the attacks pose a direct threat to civilian lives and safety, constitute a dangerous escalation threatening the security of energy supplies, international trade and navigation, and undermine regional security and stability. Bahrain reaffirmed its full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its unwavering support for all measures taken to safeguard its sovereignty, security and stability, protect its national assets and ensure the safety of its citizens and residents. It also affirmed Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to self-defense under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, stressing that the Kingdom’s security is an integral part of the security of Bahrain and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). The ministry renewed Bahrain’s call on the UN Security Council to assume its responsibilities and take firm and deterrent measures to halt repeated Houthi terrorist attacks, hold their perpetrators and supporters accountable, and ensure the full implementation of relevant resolutions, particularly resolutions 2216, 2817 and 2837. It stressed the need to protect civilians and civilian and vital facilities, ensure the continuity of global energy supplies and the freedom of international trade and maritime and air navigation, and safeguard regional and international security and stability. Both Kuwait and Bahrain expressed their sincere condolences and sympathies to the family of the deceased and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Meanwhile, Algeria condemned the indiscriminate attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, particularly its vital and civilian facilities, expressing deep concern over the repercussions of the escalation affecting countries across the region. Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf affirmed his country’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its support for the Kingdom in defending its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity. Attaf stressed that developments in the Gulf and Red Sea regions require the utmost caution and responsibility, reiterating Algeria’s solidarity with countries facing attacks or threats to their security, sovereignty and territorial integrity. The Muslim World League also strongly condemned and denounced the continued aggression by the Houthi terrorist militia against Saudi Arabia, including the attack on the Jazan oil refinery, which killed one worker and injured others of various nationalities. In a statement issued by the MWL’s General Secretariat, Secretary-General and Chairman of the Organization of Muslim Scholars Sheikh Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa renewed his denunciation of the treacherous terrorist attacks. He stressed that the attacks violate all religious values, international and humanitarian laws and norms, and demonstrate the criminal approach of the terrorist militia in deliberately targeting civilians and civilian facilities. Speaking on behalf of the MWL’s assemblies, bodies and international councils, as well as all Muslim peoples under its umbrella, Al-Issa reaffirmed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in all measures taken to deter aggressors, safeguard its security and ensure the safety of its citizens and residents.

items.title: Saudi Arabia elected to chair OIC Occupational Safety and Health Network for two-year term
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯当选为伊斯兰合作组织职业安全与健康网络主席，任期两年
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia has been elected to chair the Organization of Islamic Cooperation’s Occupational Safety and Health Network (OIC-OSHNET) for a two-year term, represented by the National Council for Occupational Safety and Health (NCOSH). The election took place during the network’s annual meeting on November 23, which brought together representatives of OIC member states and specialized international and regional organizations under the theme “Towards Shared Priorities in Occupational Safety and Health.” Members also elected Malaysia and Senegal as vice-chairs and approved the network’s governance and operational arrangements to enhance institutional coordination and technical cooperation. Under its chairmanship, Saudi Arabia will work to advance cooperation among member states, establish common priorities, develop occupational risk prevention initiatives and expand capacity-building programs and the exchange of expertise. **media[2800550]** During the meeting, the Kingdom outlined its efforts to strengthen its national occupational safety and health system, highlighting NCOSH’s regulatory and coordination role and its regional contributions through the Gulf Strategic Framework for Occupational Safety and Health (2025–2030). The chairmanship builds on Saudi Arabia’s efforts to improve workplace safety through legislative development, preventive measures and greater compliance with occupational safety and health requirements, in line with Saudi Vision 2030. Participating organizations included the International Labour Organization (ILO), the International Social Security Association (ISSA), the International Organisation of Employers (IOE) and the European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA). Operating under the OIC Labour Centre, the network brings together 57 member states to address occupational risks through joint initiatives, knowledge sharing and the development of institutional and technical capabilities.

items.title: Coalition destroys 50 Houthi military targets and ballistic missile launcher in Yemen
items.title_zh: 联军在也门摧毁50个胡塞武装军事目标和弹道导弹发射架
items.summary: RIYADH — Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, said that a precision military operation was carried out to target the capabilities of the terrorist Houthi militia."We destroyed 50 legitimate military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah, and Saada governorates,” he said. Al-Maliki also stated that the Coalition forces have destroyed a ballistic missile launcher in Hodeidah that the terrorist Houthi militia used in its attack on Jazan refinery on Thursday.

items.title: Saudi Arabia strongly condemns Iranian aggression on Kuwait
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯强烈谴责伊朗对科威特的侵略
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed Saudi Arabia's condemnation and denunciation in the strongest terms of Iran's heinous aggression against Kuwait, which targeted a vital site, resulting in several deaths and injuries. In a statement, the ministry said: “The continued Iranian attacks lead to further tensions and instability. The Kingdom reiterates that these violations undermine international efforts aimed at restoring security and stability in the region.”Saudi Arabia held Iran responsible for the consequences of its continued brutal attacks. It demanded an immediate cessation of these violations while reaffirming its full solidarity with Kuwait in all measures it takes to safeguard its sovereignty.

items.title: King Salman and Crown Prince offer condolences to Egyptian president over Giza fire tragedy
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王和王储就吉萨火灾悲剧向埃及总统表示慰问
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman have offered condolences to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi over the victims of the fire in Al-Warraq district in the Giza governorate.In separate cables sent to El-Sisi, the King and the Crown Prince expressed their deepest condolences and sincere sympathy to the president, the families of the deceased, and the people of Egypt. They prayed to God Almighty to bestow His abundant mercy and forgiveness upon the deceased, grant their families patience and solace, bless the injured with a speedy recovery, and protect the president and the people of Egypt from all harm. Thirty-one people have been killed, with another 21 injured, after a fuel truck overturned sparking a huge fire. The incident occurred when a truck was traveling from Cairo’s El-Marg district on the Warraq Ring Road near Giza, about 12 miles away from the famous Great Pyramid, on the evening of Wednesday.
